instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: By AD 48, the Roman army had conquered most of southern and eastern Britain. However, their progress slowed as they reached the steep hills, rivers and dense forests of modern-day Wales.
Paired with the fierce resistance of the local tribes, the Romans focused on securing their existing power rather than expanding their territory further.

However, from AD 58, now under the rule of Emperor Nero, the Romans began to move again. The army started in the south of Wales and slowly marched north. As they advanced, the Britons fled from the fighting. Lots of these people ended up on the island of Anglesey, right in the north-west corner of Wales.

atoms.a: Which two factors slowed the Roman invasion into Wales?
Why did many people move to Anglesey?
b: ++They were forced north by the Romans.

feedback.finish: One reason the Romans continued their invasion into Wales was to take advantage of the valuable metals in the Welsh hills.

instruction.text: What did the Romans use these metals for? Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: The Romans used lead for making water pipes.
atoms.sound: The Romans used led for making water pipes.

hint.text: The Latin word for lead is plumbum. As the Romans used lead to make water pipes, this is where the word “plumbing” comes from!
hint.sound: The Latin word for lead is plumbum. As the Romans used led to make water pipes, this is where the word “plumbing” comes from!
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.a: Coins were made out of silver, copper and gold.
The Romans often wore jewellery made from gold, silver and copper.

feedback.end: Anglesey was also a holy place for druids, who were important figures in Celtic religion and society.

atoms.b: We druids believe that nature is full of power and we worship ((++Celtic Roman)) gods and goddesses.

We have many important responsibilities in our communities. We teach children, give ((++advice homework)) to leaders, act as ((++judges bullies)) in disagreements and help people by healing them with ((++plants antibiotics)).
Due to our various roles, most Britons look to us for guidance, and we have a lot of ((++power fun)) and influence.

instruction.text: Listen and select the correct answer.

atoms.a: Why do you think the Romans saw the druids as a threat?

b.sound: The druids could encourage tribes to fight together against Rome.
The druids had a huge army the Romans could not defeat.

feedback.end: United tribes could have caused a lot of trouble for the Romans, so they decided they had to defeat the druids to secure their control over the area.

hint.text: Everything we know about the invasion of Anglesey comes from one writer: the Roman historian Tacitus. He wrote about this around 50 years after it happened, so we probably shouldn’t believe everything he wrote!
hint.sound: Everything we know about the invasion of Anglesey comes from one writer: the Roman historian Tacithus. He wrote about this around 50 years after it happened, so we probably shouldn’t believe everything he wrote!
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.b: In AD 60, the Romans crossed the small stretch of ((++water road)) to Anglesey.
They faced a line of druids waving torches and yelling curses at the Romans. The sight scared the Romans at first, but they ((++continued stopped)) the attack.
The Roman army killed the druids, burned the sacred groves and ((++destroyed protected)) places for religious ceremonies.

feedback.finish: The Romans’ victory was cut short as news arrived about an uprising in the south-east of Britain, forcing the Roman army to leave Anglesey quickly. Wales was later conquered in its entirety in AD 77.
